title: Subagents cannot access chat image attachments available to the parent agent
body:
**Problem:**  
Images attached to a VS Code agent-chat message are visible to the parent agent, but background subagents cannot read those same attachments from the filesystem paths supplied by the runtime.

The paths are under:

```text
Code - Insiders/agentSessionData/<session>/attachments/
```

The subagent’s file tools treat this directory as content-excluded. Consequently, tasks such as delegating a visual comparison fail even though the parent agent can view the images directly.

**Expected behavior:**  
A subagent delegated by the parent should receive safe access to user-provided attachments, ideally through copied session-scoped files or inherited attachment context.

**Actual behavior:**  
The subagent can see the attachment paths in its prompt but cannot open them. It must stop due to content-exclusion policy.

**Impact:**  
Users cannot reliably delegate image analysis, screenshot comparisons, or other attachment-based work to subagents.

**Suggested improvement:**  
When launching a subagent, make user-approved attachments available through a readable, session-scoped artifact path or pass them as native multimodal context.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?:No

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.130.0 
- OS Version:  macOS 15

**Bug -  enterprise policy / MCP governance**
The `ChatAllowedMcpServers` policy (added in #326226) is deployed via managed
settings (macOS configuration profile / Windows registry) with a single allowed
stdio command, e.g.:
    "ChatAllowedMcpServers": [
      { "serverCommand": ["npx", "--yes", "my-approved-mcp-server"] }
    ]
Confirmed applied via `Developer: Policy Diagnostics` (shows the resolved value)
and it behaves correctly for the built-in agent.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Apply the policy above so only the one approved `serverCommand` is allowed.
2. Add a second, non-approved MCP server to `mcp.json` (any other stdio command,
   or a marketplace-installed MCP server).
3. In a chat session using the **local** agent, ask the model to call a tool
   from the non-approved server.
   → Correctly **blocked**: the server never connects and the tool call is
     rejected ("blocked by policy"). 
4. Switch the same session to the **delegated agent-host runtime** (the
   "Local" → Copilot session toggle; the agent-host integration from #320854).
5. Ask for the same tool call again.
**Expected**
The `ChatAllowedMcpServers` allowlist should apply regardless of which runtime
executes the session. The non-approved server should be blocked in the
agent-host session exactly as it is in the local agent.
**Actual**
In the delegated agent-host session the non-approved MCP server **connects and
its tools are fully callable** - the allowlist is not consulted. `MCP: List
Servers` for the agent-host session shows the non-approved server as **Running**.
Removing the policy makes no difference; re-selecting the local agent blocks it
again.
### Impact
`ChatAllowedMcpServers` is an enterprise **security** control. Any user can
bypass it - and run an otherwise-blocked MCP server - with a single click that
delegates the session to the agent host. Administrators have no way to detect or
prevent this from the policy artifacts themselves.
### Related
- #326226 (added the `ChatAllowedMcpServers` / `ChatDeniedMcpServers` policies)
- #320854 (agent-host session MCP integration)

title: feat: per-agent skill scoping, add `skills:` to `.agent.md` frontmatter
body: Resolves #307630 ## Summary Adds a `skills:` frontmatter field on custom agents (`.agent.md`) so authors can control which skills appear in that agent’s model-invocable skill catalog. Similar to `tools:` field. This change makes loop engineering easier with vscode-copilot (I'm not sure how copilot cloud agents work), allowing minimal session context on specialized agents, specially for teams using monorepos with lots of shared skills. It also gets vscode-copilot closer to the capabilities offered by other harnesses like Codex and Open Code that already provide this feature. This is different than Claude Code's `skills:` which means "preloaded skills into subagent context", which I recommend to be implemented in vscode/copilot as field named `preload-skills` (#293752). ### Semantics | Value | Behavior | |-------|----------| | omit `skills` | All model-invocable skills (backward compatible) | | `skills: []` | No skills in the catalog | | `skills: [a, b]` | Only skills named `a` / `b` (that also pass existing filters) | | `skills: ['*']` | Explicit all | Existing per-skill filters still apply after the whitelist (`disable-model-invocation`, required description, session type, etc.). Unknown skill names do not fail agent load; the editor reports a warning. ### Implementation - Parse `skills` on `PromptHeader` (sequence or comma-separated scalar) - Thread through `ICustomAgent.skills` → `CustomChatMode.customSkills` - Filter catalog in core `ComputeAutomaticInstructions` and Copilot `AutomaticInstructionsCollector` - Expose `allowedSkills` on `ChatRequestModeInstructions` for the extension path - Editor: attribute metadata, completion from `findAgentSkills()`, validation, hovers - Docs: agent-customization skill reference ### Tests - Parser: sequence / empty / `*` / scalar / omit - Catalog filter: undefined / `[]` / `['*']` / subset / `disableModelInvocation` - Mode refresh of `customSkills` - Prompts service header plumbing - Extension collector `allowedSkills` filter | Before | After | |-|-| ||| ||| | Autocomplete | |-| ||

title: fix: gate chat tips on registered commands to prevent 'openPlan' command not found (fixes #328231)

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
### Summary

Clicking the **Plan mode** chat tip throws `command 'workbench.action.chat.openPlan' not found` (bucket `07b425dd-be0d-a662-1409-6bb227df5a7b`, ~1,552 users on 1.131.0). The tip in `chatTipCatalog.ts` renders a markdown link `command:workbench.action.chat.openPlan`, but that command is **not registered** in shipped builds — it only exists on an unmerged feature branch. When the user clicks the rendered link, `openerService` routes it to `commandService._tryExecuteCommand`, which throws because the command is unknown, and the error reaches error telemetry.

The fix is producer-side: the tip service decides which tips are eligible to show, so we gate eligibility on whether every `command:` link the tip renders is actually registered. A tip referencing an unregistered command is never shown, so the dead link is never presented and the error path is never reached. This is general and defends against any future stale command reference in the tip catalog.

Fixes microsoft/vscode\#328231
Recommended reviewer: `@meganrogge`

### Culprit Commit

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Commit | `3d374070c9a` (message text later tweaked in `3623d50299a8`) |
| PR | #298271 "improve tip service" |
| Author | `@meganrogge` |
| What it did | Shipped the `tip.planMode` entry referencing `command:workbench.action.chat.openPlan`. The `openPlan` command itself was only added on an unmerged branch (`347fffeb87f`), so it never shipped — leaving the tip pointing at a non-existent command. |

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[ChatTipService shows tip.planMode] --> B[chatTipContentPart renders markdown]
  B --> C[User clicks command:workbench.action.chat.openPlan link]
  C --> D[chatTipContentPart._handleTipAction]
  D --> E[openerService.open]
  E --> F[commandService._tryExecuteCommand]
  F --> G{command registered?}
  G -- no --> H[throw command 'openPlan' not found -> error telemetry]
```

### Affected Files

| File | Role | Evidence |
|------|------|----------|
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatTipCatalog.ts` | Producer of the offending reference | `tip.planMode` renders `command:workbench.action.chat.openPlan`, a command not registered in shipped code |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatTipService.ts` | Eligibility gate (fix location) | `_isEligible` decides which tips are shown; extended to exclude tips with unregistered commands |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatTipContentPart.ts` | Crash-site frame (not modified) | `_handleTipAction` forwards the link to `openerService` |
| `src/vs/workbench/services/commands/common/commandService.ts` | Crash site (not modified) | `_tryExecuteCommand` throws "command not found" |

### Repro Steps

1. Run a shipped 1.131.0 build (where `workbench.action.chat.openPlan` is not registered).
2. Trigger the chat panel such that the Plan mode tip is shown in the tip content part.
3. Click the tip's action link.
4. Observe `command 'workbench.action.chat.openPlan' not found` thrown via `commandService._tryExecuteCommand` and reported to error telemetry.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** — `chatTipService.ts`: added `_areTipCommandsRegistered(tip)` and a call to it in `_isEligible` before returning `true`. The method builds the tip message, extracts every `command:` id via the existing `extractCommandIds()` helper, and returns `false` (logging a debug line) if any id is missing from `CommandsRegistry.getCommand()`. This fixes the bug at the data producer — the tip service that produces the shown tip — rather than at the crash site in `commandService`. It does not add any `try/catch` and does not remove or alter `logService.error` calls, so the telemetry pipeline is untouched; it simply prevents an invalid tip (one pointing at a non-existent command) from ever being produced. Because `registerAction2` registers into `CommandsRegistry`, this correctly detects all real chat mode-open commands (Ask/Agent/Edit) as registered while excluding the unregistered `openPlan`.

**Alternatives considered**:
- Register a no-op/real `openPlan` command — rejected: the command's real implementation lives on an unmerged branch; shipping a stand-in would mask the missing feature and could mislead users who click it.
- Guard/`try-catch` at `commandService._tryExecuteCommand` — rejected: that is the crash site, not the producer, and swallowing the throw would hide errors from the telemetry pipeline.
- Remove the `tip.planMode` entry outright — rejected: narrower but doesn't prevent the general class of stale command references; the eligibility gate covers this and any future catalog drift.

### Recommended Owner

`@meganrogge` — authored the tip catalog entry and the tip service (commit `3d374070c9a`, PR #298271), and is an active VS Code team member with recent commits in this area (chat/voice). Best positioned to review whether the Plan mode tip should instead ship with a registered command.

title: fix: wait for transient SQLite locks in ExternalIngestIndex (fixes #328227)
body:
### Summary

The copilot-chat extension throws an unhandled `Error: database is locked` (SQLITE_BUSY) from `ExternalIngestIndex`. The crash surfaces in the file-watcher event handler `onFileChanged` → `tryAddOrUpdateFile` → `get`, when a synchronous `SELECT` runs against the per-workspace `codebase-external.sqlite` file while another connection holds a write lock.

The root cause is a connection-setup gap: the SQLite connections are never given a busy timeout, so any transient lock contention immediately raises `SQLITE_BUSY` instead of briefly waiting. Because the same per-workspace database file can be opened by more than one VS Code window (and by more than one embedding-type `CodeSearchChunkSearch` in a window), brief write overlaps are expected and should be tolerated. Additionally, the existing-database open path applied none of the connection PRAGMAs that the fresh-database path applied, so an existing DB got an even more default (fail-fast) locking configuration.

The error escapes to telemetry because the reads happen inside event-driven handlers (`onFileChanged`/`onFileAdded`) that are not — and should not be — wrapped in error suppression. The correct fix is at the data producer: the connection configuration.

Fixes microsoft/vscode\#328227
Recommended reviewer: `@mjbvz`

### Culprit Commit

Not precisely bisected within the time budget. The `ExternalIngestIndex` SQLite layer is authored/owned by `@mjbvz` (all GDPR `owner` tags in the file are `mjbvz`); the bug is inherent to the connection-setup code (`openOrCreateDatabase` / `createFreshDatabase`) rather than a single regressing line. Marked `recent-regression` on the issue, consistent with the external-ingest feature being recently enabled for more resources (see nearby commits "Enable external ingest for non-file resources too").

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Another window / connection holds write lock on codebase-external.sqlite] --> B[File watcher fires onDidChange]
  B --> C[onFileChanged uri]
  C --> D[tryAddOrUpdateFile uri]
  D --> E[get uri : synchronous SELECT via _db.prepare.get]
  E --> F{Connection has busy_timeout?}
  F -- No default 0 --> G[SQLITE_BUSY: database is locked thrown to telemetry]
  F -- Yes 5000ms --> H[Waits for lock to clear, query succeeds]
```

### Affected Files

- `extensions/copilot/src/platform/workspaceChunkSearch/node/codeSearch/externalIngestIndex.ts` — add a `busy_timeout` PRAGMA to every connection opened by the index (both the existing-database open path and the fresh-database creation path).

### Repro Steps

1. Open the same workspace/folder in two VS Code windows with the copilot-chat extension active and workspace chunk search / external ingest enabled.
2. Let both windows initialize `ExternalIngestIndex` against the shared `codebase-external.sqlite`.
3. Modify files in the workspace so the file watchers fire `onDidChange` in both windows concurrently while one connection is mid-write.
4. Observe `Error: database is locked` from `ExternalIngestIndex.get` in telemetry / the extension log.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** (`externalIngestIndex.ts`): Introduce a single `configureBusyTimeout(db)` helper that runs `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;` and call it on every connection the index opens — both in the existing-database branch of `openOrCreateDatabase` (which previously applied no PRAGMAs at all) and in `createFreshDatabase`. This fixes the problem at the data producer (the connection configuration) rather than at the crash site: with a busy timeout set, SQLite blocks briefly and retries when it encounters a lock instead of immediately throwing `SQLITE_BUSY`, so the transient contention that the shared per-workspace file inevitably produces no longer escapes as an unhandled error. After this change, `get`'s `SELECT` at the watcher-driven call site cannot raise `database is locked` for a lock that clears within the timeout window, because the connection now waits for it instead of failing fast.

The existing constructor already falls back to an in-memory database if the initial open throws, and no `logService.error`/telemetry calls were removed — the error pipeline is untouched; only the fail-fast locking behavior of healthy connections is corrected. No `try/catch` was added around the crash site.

**Alternatives considered**:
- Wrapping `get`/`tryAddOrUpdateFile` in `try/catch` to swallow the error — rejected because it hides the contention at the consumer crash site instead of fixing the producer connection configuration, and would silently drop legitimate index updates.
- Serializing all DB access behind a mutex — rejected as heavier than needed; the contention is cross-connection/cross-window, which an in-process lock cannot solve, whereas `busy_timeout` addresses exactly the cross-connection case.

### Recommended Owner

`@mjbvz` — owner of all GDPR telemetry annotations in `externalIngestIndex.ts` and author of the external-ingest SQLite layer.

title: fix: require models field in ModelList validator (fixes #328226)
body:
### Summary `get nesModels` in `ProxyModelsService` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'filter')` because `this._models.models` is `undefined` while `this._models` itself is defined. This happens when the `/models` proxy endpoint returns a JSON object that lacks the `models` key: the response validator treats `models` as optional and produces `{ models: undefined }`, which violates the `ModelList.t` type contract (`models: Model.t[]`). The getter then calls `.filter` on `undefined`. Impact: 7.1x spike (44 → 314 affected users) across the 0.56.0 → 0.58.0 range, predominantly macOS. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#328226 Recommended reviewer: `@ulugbekna` ### Culprit Commit This is a pre-existing type-contract defect in the validation layer, surfaced (not introduced) by the recent spike. The `ModelList` validator has declared `models` without `vRequired` since it was introduced. | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`3c78ed8`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/3c78ed81dda850fa78544e8ff737955660faf440) | | Author | `@ulugbekna` | | PR | #2325 | | Message | nes: support /models on proxy and model picker | | Why | Introduced `ModelList.validator = vObj({ models: vArray(...) })` without `vRequired`. Because `vObj` skips validation for non-required fields that are missing, a `/models` response without a `models` key validates successfully to `{ models: undefined }`, violating the declared `ModelList.t` type. The runtime spike appears to be a server-side response-shape change; the bypass that lets the bad shape through is this validator. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Server as /models endpoint participant Fetch as _fetchLatestModels participant Validator as ModelList.validator participant Store as this._models participant Getter as get nesModels Server->>Fetch: JSON without "models" key Fetch->>Validator: validate(jsonData) Note over Validator: ⚠️ Root cause:
models not vRequired →
missing field skipped →
returns { models: undefined } Validator->>Store: this._models = { models: undefined } Store->>Getter: onModelListUpdated fires Note over Getter: 💥 this._models?.models.filter(...)
undefined.filter → TypeError ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/proxyModels/node/proxyModelsService.ts` | crash site | L68: `return this._models?.models.filter(...)` | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/inlineEdits/common/dataTypes/inlineEditsModelsTypes.ts` | root cause | L47-L49: `validator = vObj({ models: vArray(Model.validator) })` — `models` not marked required | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/configuration/common/validator.ts` | bypass mechanism | L138-L143: `vObj` skips non-required fields that are `undefined`, so a missing `models` passes validation | ### Repro Steps 1. Configure the proxy `/models` endpoint (or a mock) to return a JSON object that omits the `models` key (e.g. `{}` or `{ "someOtherKey": 1 }`). 2. Trigger a Copilot token store update so the `autorun` in `ProxyModelsService` fetches `/models`. 3. The response validates to `{ models: undefined }` and is stored in `this._models`, then `onModelListUpdated` fires. 4. The `inlineEditsModelService` observable reads `proxyModelsService.nesModels`, invoking the getter → `undefined.filter` → `TypeError`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/inlineEdits/common/dataTypes/inlineEditsModelsTypes.ts`): wrap the `models` field validator in `vRequired`: `models: vRequired(vArray(Model.validator))`. This fixes the defect at the data producer (the validator that constructs the `ModelList.t` value), not at the crash site. With `models` required, a `/models` response missing the key now fails validation; `_fetchLatestModels` takes its existing error branch (`throw new Error('Invalid /models response data: ...')`), which is caught and reported through the existing `logService.error` telemetry path, and `_models` is never assigned an object whose `models` is `undefined`. title: Support offline dictation model install for registry-blocked networks
body: Fixes #328154 ## Problem On-device dictation (Foundry Local / Nemotron ASR) provisions its native runtime fine through a corporate proxy, but the **model download** fails. The native downloader first resolves the model through the Azure ML **registry** (`api.catalog.azureml.ms` + per-region registry endpoints) to get a signed blob URI, and only then downloads the bytes. Locked-down networks block those registry endpoints, so it fails with `RegionFallbackException` / TLS errors across all regions before ever reaching the blob CDN. This is endpoint blocking, not a proxy misconfig, so there is no settings-level fix. The model files themselves are separately published on a reachable Microsoft download CDN as an expansion-pack ZIP. Foundry Local's SDK has a local scanner: if the files exist in the cache in the right layout (with `genai_config.json` + `inference_model.json`), `model.isCached` becomes `true` and `download()` short-circuits, never touching the registry. ## What this PR does 1. **New command** `Chat: Install Dictation Model from Local Package...` — imports the official Foundry Local expansion pack (ZIP or extracted OCI layout) or a prepared model directory into the dictation model cache, writing the scanner metadata that makes Foundry Local treat the model as cached. Gated on `ChatContextKeys.enabled` + `dictation.enabled`. 2. **Discoverable recovery** — when a model download fails with a network/registry error (`errorCode` = `network`/`notFound`), the failure notification surfaces an **"Install from Local Package..."** action that launches the same command, so users find the fix exactly when they hit the wall. Other failures are unchanged. The importer validates the package (rejects path-traversal in OCI layer titles and wrong-model packages), stages into a temp dir and atomically swaps into place with backup/rollback, and moves (rather than copies) files extracted to temp to avoid transient disk bloat. ## Why not fully auto-download? The reachable CDN URL isn't a published/stable contract, the blob is large, and stricter lockdowns can block that host too — auto-fetch would just relocate the failure and add downloader bulk. The guided import gets the benefit without the fragility. ## Notes on bulk No new npm dependencies. Reuses the existing `localTranscription` utility process and `base/node/zip.ts` (yauzl) extractor plus Node built-ins. The importer code loads only when the command runs. ## Validation - `transpile-client`, `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check` — clean - New importer tests + zip regression — 10/10 passing (prepared dir import, nested OCI expansion-pack import, path-traversal rejection, wrong-model rejection) - Hygiene — clean Also fixes a pre-existing disposable leak in `base/node/zip.ts` (the cancellation listener in `extractEntry` was never disposed).

title: Support custom views inside the agents window workbench
body:
Give the Agents window a way to show a full-surface, session-independent screen (a dashboard-style view such as the upcoming Automations view) in place of the sessions grid, without inventing a new UI shell each time.

How it works: a new CustomViewGridPart sits in the workbench grid next to the sessions part, and contributions register an ICustomViewDescriptor (id, title, view constructor, optional header actions) with ICustomViewService, then call showCustomView(id). The workbench observes activeCustomView and, in one atomic pass, renders the view, swaps the grid nodes and moves focus — the sessions grid, the in-grid editor, the side panel and the bottom panel are hidden while the custom view is up, and exactly one of the two grids always owns the row.

Those covered parts keep their desired visibility rather than being genuinely toggled off, so hiding the custom view restores whatever the layout controller last wanted, including changes made in the background. Opening a session dismisses the custom view automatically, and the actions that operate on the hidden parts (Toggle Side Panel, Open Terminal, secondary side bar) are disabled while it is shown.

Each view is hosted in a CustomViewNode that owns the shared chrome — title, optional description, a toolbar or button bar, and a scroll container whose header grows a border once scrolled — so a view only implements render() and layout(). The node's content is centred and capped to the same measure the session views use, overridable per view, and the part reuses the sessions part's card class and metrics so the two surfaces are visually identical. Nothing is persisted, so a reload always starts on the sessions grid.

title: markdown: fix: route undo and redo to the document history
body:
Wires undo/redo into the core Markdown editor (viewType `vscode.markdown.editor`) so `Cmd+Z` / `Cmd+Shift+Z` work in the Agents window. Closes #327535.

### Problem

The experimental hybrid Markdown editor is a `CustomTextEditorProvider` whose webview embeds `@vscode/markdown-editor` and attaches an `EditContext`. Because of the `EditContext`, the browser keeps no native undo history and the history chords never reach VS Code's command routing, so `Cmd+Z` does nothing today. The `TextDocument` behind the custom editor already has a full undo stack — it just isn't wired up.

### Change

- **`markdown-editor-src/editor.ts`** — pass a `historyStrategy` to `EditorController` that posts `{ type: 'history', command: 'undo' | 'redo' }` to the extension. `record` is intentionally **not** implemented: the `TextDocument` is the single source of truth, and a second local stack would drift from the Edit menu, dirty state and hot exit.
- **`markdownEditorProvider.ts`** — handle the `history` message by executing the built-in `undo`/`redo` command (guarded to just those two). It first `await`s the existing `editQueue` so any in-flight edit lands before history runs, and only acts while `webviewPanel.active`, so a message delivered after an editor switch can't undo a different document. `CustomEditorService` registers priority-105 `UndoCommand`/`RedoCommand` implementations that route to the active custom editor input's resource-scoped `IUndoRedoService`, ahead of the generic webview implementation (priority 100), so the chord hits this document's history. (Verified against `src/vs/workbench/contrib/customEditor/browser/customEditors.ts` and `customEditorInput.ts`.)
- **`markdown-editor-src/editor.ts`** (`update` handler) — apply the authoritative host text with `model.replaceSourceText(...)` instead of `sourceText.set(...)`, so the selection is mapped through the changed span (the caret could otherwise land out of range after an undo shrinks the document) and stale pending-paragraph state is cleared atomically. The existing `isUpdatingFromExtension` guard still prevents the update from echoing back as an edit.
- **`package.json` / `package-lock.json`** — bump `@vscode/markdown-editor` to **`0.0.2-40`**, the published release that ships the `IHistoryStrategy` / `EditorControllerOptions.historyStrategy` and `EditorModel.replaceSourceText` APIs used above.

Result: keyboard, the Edit menu and the Command Palette all share one history — the `TextDocument`'s.

### Dependency

The consumed `@vscode/markdown-editor` APIs were added by **microsoft/vscode-packages#189** and are published as `0.0.2-40`, which this PR pins (rebased on top of `main`, which had bumped to `0.0.2-37`). The dependency set is unchanged and the lockfile integrity matches the published tarball.

### Testing

- Typechecked `markdown-editor-src` and the extension-host `src` against the installed `0.0.2-40` declarations — both clean.
- No unit tests exist for this provider. Manual smoke test: open a `.md` in the Agents window, ensure Editing mode, put the caret after `abc`, type `d`, press `Cmd+Z` (→ `abc`), `Cmd+Shift+Z` (→ `abcd`); confirm **Edit > Undo** does the same and the caret lands sensibly.

title: Voice: queue concurrent question forms instead of swapping them
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8624

Follow-on to #327899, which made a spoken answer land on the right question form. That fix assumed one form at a time; with two pending in the same session it picks the wrong one.

## The bug

Two functions independently decide which pending part voice is working on, and both took the **last** match: `_getAgentStateInfo` (the spoken `agent_state_detail`) and `_buildPendingPayload` (the structured `pending` an answer is resolved against). A second form arriving silently stole focus, so the user mid-answer on form A had their next utterance resolved against form B.

Fixing only the payload would be worse than the bug: `_getAgentStateInfo` would still hold the newest, its changed detail alone satisfies `isDetailTransition`, and the narration it triggers reads the payload and gets A. Questions aren't text-deduped, so form A would be re-read aloud every time B arrived. Both callers have to agree.

## The fix

One `_selectPendingPart`, used by both, scanning **oldest-first** and returning the first still-open part. A form holds focus until it resolves; a second form waits its turn. This also matches the platform — `chatModel._pendingInfo` scans forward and its value already feeds the fallback `_getAgentStateInfo` uses. Newest-first was the deviation.

Split so the two callers can't drift again: `_selectPendingPart` (which part), `_isOpenPendingPart` (still open, per kind), `_describePendingPart` (the prose, lifted verbatim).

## Also here

Send each session's `label`. The backend renders `[SESSIONS]` for its routing model and refuses to guess between waiting sessions — but every entry we sent was anonymous, so two concurrent forms arrived as two identical lines.

Drop `active_session`. The only place that would assign it is an empty `try {} catch {}`, so it has always been undefined and the delta never carried the field — removal is provably behaviour-preserving. The per-entry `is_active` flag names the focused session.

## Verification

`VoiceSessionController` + `VoiceClientService`: **73 passing**, 11 new — oldest-first selection, moving on once a form resolves, an executing tool not shadowing the form it opened, an older form surviving a newer arrival, payload and spoken detail agreeing, a newer form answered by mouse leaving focus untouched, and the session labels. Compile is clean in `contrib/chat` (the 90 total errors are pre-existing on `main`, in `platform/agentHost`, `localTranscription` and `native`).

Draft until the companion backend change lands and the two-form case has been driven end to end by voice.

title: sessions: keep feedback submit overlay inside diff
body:
## Summary

Keep the Agent Feedback submit/navigation toolbar visually and structurally owned by the diff editor when the Agents window uses the single-pane layout.

- Anchor the overlay to the inset editor pane instead of the full editor group.
- Add focused lifecycle/host regression coverage.
- Add a dark/light integrated fixture with a real multi-diff, the production overlay controller, and a docked Files panel.

## Root cause

The single-pane layout has two different horizontal bounds:

```text
Editor group:  [──────────── diff ────────────|──── Files detail ────]
Editor pane:   [──────────── diff ────────────]
```

The group intentionally spans both regions so the tab bar can span the entire side pane. However, `EditorGroupView.layout()` narrows `editorContainer` by `_contentRightInset`:

```ts
const contentWidth = width - this._contentRightInset;
this.editorContainer.style.width = `${contentWidth}px`;
```

The feedback overlay was appended to the **full group** and positioned with:

```ts
position: absolute;
right: 24px;
bottom: 24px;
```

Therefore, `right: 24px` meant “24px from the right edge of the Files panel,” not “24px from the right edge of the diff.” The overlay code predated the single-pane layout; its assumption that group width equaled editor width stopped being true once the detail panel was docked inside the editor part.

## Changes

### Expose the correct host

`EditorGroupView` now exposes its editor-pane container:

```ts
get editorPaneContainer(): HTMLElement {
	return this.editorContainer;
}
```

`editorContainer` was already the authoritative DOM element whose width excludes the docked detail inset. Exposing this narrow API lets editor-content overlays follow the existing geometry automatically when the detail panel resizes, hides, or changes which editor group receives the right inset.

### Let the overlay controller own host selection

The controller now accepts an editor-group contract that includes `editorPaneContainer` and chooses the host itself:

```ts
const container = group.editorPaneContainer;
```

The production call site therefore passes only the group instead of supplying `group.element`. This prevents callers from accidentally selecting the full-width group again.

The small structural `IAgentFeedbackOverlayEditorGroup` interface also lets the component fixture instantiate the real production controller without copying or recomposing the toolbar.

### Establish the CSS containing block

The selected pane receives a scoped host class:

```css
.agent-feedback-editor-overlay-host {
	position: relative;
}
```

Appending an absolutely positioned child is not sufficient by itself: without a positioned pane, the overlay can still resolve against a wider positioned ancestor. The controller adds this class during construction and removes it through its disposable store.

I deliberately did not globally make every editor container positioned, because that could alter the containing block for unrelated absolute children.

### Add focused unit coverage

The new test uses a real `EditorGroupView`:

1. Record the full editor-pane width.
2. Apply a simulated 300px docked-detail inset.
3. Instantiate the real workbench contribution.
4. Verify that the pane width shrinks by 300px.
5. Verify that the pane—not the full group—owns the overlay host class.
6. Dispose the contribution and verify the host class is removed.

This covers both the geometry contract and lifecycle cleanup.

### Add an integrated screenshot fixture

`CompactDiffWithSubmitOverlay` extends the existing Agents multi-diff fixture and renders:

- a real `MultiDiffEditorWidget`;
- the production `AgentFeedbackOverlayController`;
- one accepted feedback item, producing `1/1 ↑ ↓ Submit 1 Clear`;
- a production-shaped full-width editor group;
- a narrower editor pane;
- a docked Files panel;
- dark and light variants.

The fixture intentionally keeps the multi-diff real while simplifying only the neighboring Files content, because this regression depends on the detail-panel boundary rather than the internal Files tree implementation.

The existing `CompactDiffWithFeedback` variant remains intact and continues to cover the line-number feedback affordance.

## Visual/geometry proof

With the fix, the fixture measured:

```text
Editor pane:  x=304, right=884
Files panel:  x=884, right=1164
Overlay:      x≈637, right=860
```

So the overlay remains 24px inside the pane and ends before the detail boundary.

I also simulated the previous host by moving the same production overlay under the full group:

```text
Overlay:      x≈917, right=1140
Files panel:  x=884, right=1164
```

That places the toolbar inside Files and reproduces the reported failure.

## Why this approach

This fixes ownership rather than compensating for coordinates. It does **not**:

- subtract a hard-coded detail width;
- depend on the Sessions layout service from Agent Feedback;
- special-case multi-diff editors;
- change Submit commands or behavior;
- globally reposition every editor container;
- copy the toolbar implementation into the fixture;
- use timeout-based layout correction.

## Documentation

The single-pane layout specification and Sessions development guidance now record the invariant:

> Editor-content overlays anchor to the inset editor pane, not the full editor group.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- targeted hygiene checks
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/agentFeedback/test/browser/agentFeedbackEditorOverlay.test.ts` (`2 passing`)
- dark fixture render
- light fixture render
- browser geometry assertions
- explicit simulation of the previous group-root host
- two independent local code reviews, both with no significant findings

title: Fix hidden chat list measurement in the Agents window
body:
## Summary

Fixes #328200.

Hidden chat transcripts in the Agents window were still treated as visible by `ChatWidget`. Model updates therefore refreshed the dynamic-height chat tree under a `display:none` ancestor and emitted repeated:

```text
Measured item node at 0px- ensure that ListView is not display:none before measuring row height!
```

This change:

- combines the outer Sessions part visibility with each `SessionView` internal-grid leaf visibility;
- forwards that effective visibility through `SessionView` and `ChatView` to `ChatWidget.setVisible`;
- seeds the current visibility whenever a hosted chat view or grid slot is created;
- keeps active-session state independent, so inactive but visible side-by-side sessions continue rendering;
- documents the visibility lifecycle and adds focused regression tests.

## Root cause analysis

The warning stack maps to:

`ChatViewModel.onDidChange` -> `ChatWidget.onDidChangeItems` -> `ChatListWidget.refresh` -> `WorkbenchObjectTree.setChildren` -> `ListView.probeDynamicHeightForItem`.

The measured row remained connected to `document.body`, but a SplitView ancestor had removed its `.visible` class, whose CSS applies `display:none`.

The Sessions Grid introduced two nested visibility boundaries without forwarding either one to the chat widget:

1. `SessionView` is a leaf in the Sessions part's internal `SerializableGrid`. Maximizing one session hides sibling leaves and invokes the optional `setVisible` lifecycle hook, but `SessionView` did not implement it.
2. The outer workbench grid can hide the entire Sessions part, notably when the editor is maximized. `SessionsPart` received that lifecycle change but did not propagate it to its internal views.

At the same time, `ChatView` called `ChatWidget.setVisible(true)` once during construction and never sent `false`. Consequently, `ChatWidget._visible` remained true and its intended hidden-rendering guards never engaged.

The Sessions-specific regression entered with the Sessions Grid change in 6dfc9e40fbf801efd2e471c25021075ba44d161a on May 26, 2026. The reported Insiders build commit, 54917b34eaaeeec2b294c43d691fc6c1e4b86c89, is unrelated.

## Effects

- repeated console warnings and stack construction, with avoidable CPU/battery cost;
- unnecessary hidden markdown, tree, and progressive response rendering;
- transient zero-height rows that can distort content height, scrollbars, scroll anchors, and auto-scroll;
- revealed transcripts that can appear blank/collapsed or jump until remeasured;
- hidden chats performing visibility-gated actions such as scrolling to new requests;
- completed hidden sessions being marked read because `ChatWidget.visible` incorrectly remained true, suppressing unread indicators.

Chat model data is not lost and the warning itself does not crash VS Code.

## Why this fix

`ChatWidget.setVisible` is the existing lifecycle boundary designed to pause list refresh and progressive rendering while hidden, then refresh the latest model state after reveal. The fix restores that contract at the producer of the invalid measurement rather than suppressing the warning in the shared `ListView`.

The two visibility inputs are stored separately and ANDed:

- outer Sessions part visibility;
- internal grid leaf visibility.

This preserves a maximized sibling's hidden state across an outer part hide/reveal. SplitView restores the DOM-visible class before invoking `setVisible(true)`, and `ChatWidget` already defers its reveal refresh, so rows are remeasured only after the DOM is measurable.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run compile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionViewVisibility.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatView.test.ts` (6 passing)
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- targeted hygiene check for all changed TypeScript files
- pre-commit hygiene hook
- independent root-cause/design review
- independent completed-diff review with no significant findings

title: Agents: hidden chat transcripts measure dynamic rows at 0px

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
## Description

Hidden chat transcripts in the Agents window continue updating their dynamic-height list as though they were visible. While a response is streaming, this can produce many copies of:

```text
Measured item node at 0px- ensure that ListView is not display:none before measuring row height!
```

The warning stack runs through `ChatWidget.onDidChangeItems` -> `ChatListWidget.refresh` -> `WorkbenchObjectTree.setChildren` -> `ListView.probeDynamicHeightForItem`.

## Reproduction steps

1. Open the Agents window.
2. Start or observe a session whose response is actively streaming.
3. Hide that chat using either of these paths:
   - Show multiple sessions side by side, then maximize a different session.
   - Open and maximize the editor, which hides the Sessions part.
4. Keep the Developer Tools console open while the hidden chat receives updates.
5. Reveal the chat again.

## Expected behavior

When a chat's grid leaf or the containing Sessions part is hidden, the chat widget should pause DOM/list rendering. It should render the latest model state and remeasure rows after becoming visible.

## Actual behavior

The hidden chat widget remains marked visible and refreshes its dynamic-height tree under a `display:none` ancestor. Each affected row measures `0px`, logs the warning above, and can corrupt the list's transient geometry.

## Effects

- Repeated console warnings and stack construction, adding avoidable CPU/battery overhead.
- Unnecessary hidden markdown, tree, and progressive response rendering.
- Transient zero-height rows, which can distort content height, scrollbar position, scroll anchors, and auto-scroll.
- A revealed transcript can appear blank/collapsed or jump until a later remeasurement, resize, session switch, or reload repairs the geometry.
- Hidden chats can perform visibility-gated actions such as scrolling to a new request.
- A completed hidden session can be marked read because `ChatWidget.visible` incorrectly remains `true`, suppressing its unread indicator.

The chat model data itself is not lost, and this warning does not crash VS Code.

## Confirmed root cause

The Sessions Grid introduced nested visibility without forwarding that lifecycle to the chat widget:

- `ChatView` calls `ChatWidget.setVisible(true)` once and never sends `false`.
- `SessionView` is a leaf of the Sessions part's internal `SerializableGrid`, but does not implement the optional `setVisible` hook invoked when SplitView hides/maximizes a leaf.
- `SessionsPart` receives outer workbench-grid visibility changes, but does not propagate them to its internal session views.
- SplitView removes the `.visible` class before invoking the view visibility callback; its CSS gives non-visible leaves `display:none`.
- Because `ChatWidget._visible` stays `true`, model updates continue into `ChatListWidget.refresh`, where dynamic row measurement reads `offsetHeight === 0`.

The fix should combine outer Sessions-part visibility with each internal grid leaf's visibility, seed that effective value when views/slots are created, and forward it through `SessionView` and `ChatView` to `ChatWidget.setVisible`. Active-session state must remain separate because inactive side-by-side sessions are still visible.

## Regression

The Sessions-specific lifecycle regression was introduced by the Sessions Grid change in 6dfc9e40fbf801efd2e471c25021075ba44d161a on May 26, 2026.

The warning itself predates this regression and was added to diagnose dynamic-height measurement under hidden ancestors. The reported Insiders build commit, 54917b34eaaeeec2b294c43d691fc6c1e4b86c89, only changed inline completions and did not introduce the underlying issue.

## Environment

```text
Version: 1.132.0-insider (Universal)
Commit: 54917b34eaaeeec2b294c43d691fc6c1e4b86c89
Date: 2026-07-29T16:40:29Z
Electron: 42.7.1
Chromium: 148.0.7778.280
Node.js: 24.18.0
OS: Darwin arm64 25.5.0
```

Related prior workbench visibility-ordering issue: #281160. That issue addressed sidebar/panel reveal ordering; this issue is the separate nested Sessions Grid visibility propagation gap.

title: Chat: Subagent transcript items trigger potential listener leak warning

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
### Description

Opening an Agents window transcript with many surfaced subagent chats can trigger this DevTools warning:

```text
[120] potential listener LEAK detected, having 204 listeners already. MOST frequent listener (23)
```

The most frequent listener stack points through `ChatSubagentContentPart._updateOpenChatLink`, `MenuWorkbenchToolBar`, and `MenuImpl.onDidChange`.

### Reproduction steps

1. Open an Agents window session whose transcript contains many subagent tool invocations with surfaced subagent chats.
2. Let the transcript render, or scroll so its response rows rerender.
3. Open the developer tools console.
4. Observe the potential listener leak warning.

### Expected behavior

Rendered subagent transcript items should not each add a persistent listener to the shared context-key change event.

### Actual behavior

Every subagent with an openable chat creates a persistent `MenuWorkbenchToolBar` for `MenuId.ChatSubagentContent`. The toolbar listens to its `MenuImpl`, which consequently installs a listener on the shared context-key event. Completed subagent parts remain rendered in the transcript, so the listener count grows with the number of subagents and crosses the leak-warning threshold.

### Confirmed root cause

The rendered parts are correctly disposed when replaced or removed. The warning is instead caused by architectural listener fan-out: one persistent menu, and therefore one shared context-key listener, per retained `ChatSubagentContentPart`.

The subagent action is static after contribution registration, so it can be resolved using a one-shot `IMenuService.getMenuActions` snapshot and rendered in a plain `WorkbenchToolBar`. The late action-view registration race only needs a self-removing listener.

title: Preserve CRLF during partial staging
body:
Fixes #96104

Partial staging hashes the edited contents with `hash-object --path`. When `core.autocrlf` is enabled, Git applies that setting during hashing and silently converts an indexed CRLF file to LF, including lines outside the selected range.

This checks the indexed line ending with `git ls-files --eol` and disables `core.autocrlf` only while hashing files whose index form is CRLF. Other files and configured clean filters keep their existing behavior.

Tests run:

- `npm run gulp compile-extension:git` (0 errors)
- Focused CRLF partial-staging regression test (1 passing)
- Full Git extension test suite (57 passing, 2 pre-existing pending)
- Pre-commit hygiene and diff checks

title: Cascade code actions on save by provider
body:
Fixes #174295

Code action providers used for save participants were queried concurrently against the same document version, but their edits were then applied sequentially. When multiple import organizers returned edits, the later provider could apply stale offsets and duplicate or corrupt imports.

This queries and applies providers sequentially in the registry's deterministic order. Each provider therefore sees the document after the preceding provider's edits, while action ordering within a provider remains unchanged.

Tests run:

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run gulp compile` (0 errors)
- Save Participants suite (6 passing), including a regression that reproduced the duplicate import before the fix
- CodeAction suite (7 passing)
- Targeted ESLint, pre-commit hygiene, and diff checks

title: Handle unavailable restored custom editors
body:
Fixes #125582

The custom editor activation resolver always declined restoration after firing the activation event. If the provider extension was uninstalled or disabled, no later resolver claimed the input and it remained in the revival pool indefinitely.

This resolver now waits for activation and delegates to the registered provider when one becomes available. If no provider appears, restoration fails with a visible editor error and an **Open With Default Editor** recovery action instead of hanging forever.

Tests run:

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run compile-client` (0 errors)
- Targeted MainThreadCustomEditors Electron tests (2 passing)
- Pre-commit hygiene and diff checks

title: Close deinitialized Git submodules
body:
Fixes #168662

Submodule discovery used every path declared in `.gitmodules`, so a deinitialized submodule was continually treated as available and its existing Source Control repository was never closed.

This distinguishes initialized submodules by their worktree `.git` entry, closes open repositories for paths that have been deinitialized, and only schedules initialized paths for discovery. A sequence guard prevents an older asynchronous status refresh from winning a race with a newer one.

Tests run:

- `npm run gulp compile-extension:git` (0 errors)
- Focused real-repository deinit regression test (1 passing)
- Full Git extension test suite (57 passing, 2 pre-existing pending)
- Targeted ESLint, pre-commit hygiene, and diff checks

The repository-wide ESLint command also inspected generated Markdown editor output in this linked dependency setup and reported pre-existing generated-file violations; ESLint on the two changed files passed.

title: Fix large terminal paste corruption
body:
Fixes #100225

Large unbracketed multiline writes can overwhelm programs that change terminal modes while consuming input. On macOS, this was reproducible with the system Bash/readline: a 7.7 KB heredoc sent in one `node-pty` write produced a different checksum.

This change paces that input in byte-safe 256-byte chunks while preserving ordering with any writes that arrive behind it. The behavior is limited to macOS and bypasses single-line input, binary input, and bracketed paste sequences.

Tests run:

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run gulp compile-client`
- Focused `TerminalInputBuffer` unit tests (3 passing)
- Targeted ESLint and pre-commit hygiene
- Manual Bash 3.2 reproduction, repeated successfully with 256-byte/5 ms pacing

title: Feature Request: Introduce a slower release channel (e.g., Monthly/LTS) or reconsider the weekly Stable cadence

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

Since the transition to the weekly Stable release cadence starting with version 1.111, I have noticed a significant degradation in daily development stability.

While I understand the AI-induced engineering frenzy to ship features faster and faster, the compressed 7-day window does not give the extension ecosystem enough time to adapt and the quality of base vscode is taking heavy hits for months now. As a result, extensions frequently break, core editor features freeze and are way more resource hungry, and the development environment feels noticeably less reliable than it did under the previous monthly schedule. 

Treating weekly releases as the default "Stable" pipeline has made daily production work unpredictable.

The only current workaround is to manually set Update: Mode to none in settings, freeze a specific build, and entirely turn off extension auto-updates. However, manually tracking security patches and locking down the environment is a heavy maintenance burden for developers who just need a reliable tool.

I would love to see the VS Code team offer one of the following options to restore developer velocity and peace of mind:
1. Introduce a slower release channel: Create an alternate "Monthly", "Quarterly", or "LTS" channel for users who prioritize stability over bleeding-edge features. Obviously still deliver security updates in this channel.
2. Reconsider the default cadence: Pivot back to a longer testing and QA cycle for the primary Stable channel, reserving the rapid weekly cadence for an opt-in channel. It worked fine for a decade. Just go back to what worked.

VS Code used to be the absolute gold standard for code editors. It's not anymore for those of us using it in enterprise or high-stakes environments. 

Thank you for your ~~attention in this matter~~ time and hard work and the best editor ever ❤️

title: Fix subscription bug in lazy agent host start up
body:
Agent thinks it's caused by this: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/fafe3e543eca0a0c8e7e6d0443a20019bcb8385f

In short:
Previously, callers could subscribe before RemoteAgentHostProtocolClient existed. They then subscribed to a dummy event that never updated, so the agent picker stayed empty.
The change provides a permanent subscription immediately. Once the real client starts, its updates are forwarded through that same subscription. Callers no longer miss Agent Host startup.

title: Cover annotations, protocol contracts, and terminal lifecycle in agent host E2E
body:
Adds conformance coverage for Agent Host Protocol areas that no E2E test reached. Test selection came from the protocol-surface `uncovered` lists, not from chasing a percentage, and every test stays external to the host — it reaches the implementation only over AHP.

## What's covered

**`suites/annotationsSuite.ts`** — the entire `annotations/*` channel (5 actions). This was covered by neither the E2E suite nor the frozen protocol suite.

**`suites/protocolContractsSuite.ts`** — protocol-level contracts that aren't tied to one channel:
- `ping` (liveness)
- `fetchTurns` / `chat/turnsLoaded` (turn-history paging)
- `reconnect`, both the replay-gap case and the unresumable-subscription case
- the rejection contract for the four declared-but-unsupported working-directory actions

**`stateOperationsSuite.ts`** — terminal clear and exit, root's view of terminals appearing and disappearing, and queued-message promotion.

## Two things worth calling out

**`reconnect` needs a second connection.** It's only answerable on a transport that has *not* completed the handshake — it's the alternative to `initialize`, not something an established connection can issue. Calling it on the shared client returns `Method not found`. `IAgentHostE2ETestContext.connectClient` is the seam for tests that need a connection they can drop and re-establish.

**The queued-message test found undocumented behavior.** It was originally written to assert that two queued messages accumulate. They don't: a message queued onto an *idle* chat is promoted straight into a turn by `_tryConsumeNextQueuedMessage`, so the queue is empty again by the time the next action reduces.

What made this hard to see is that the dispatch envelope looked completely normal — correct `serverSeq`, no `rejectionReason` — and every other test in that suite asserts only the result of its **last** dispatch, a shape that is structurally blind to an action that is echoed but never applied. The test now asserts the real contract, and `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` records the test-shape lesson so the next author reaches for at least one cumulative assertion.

## Numbers

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Protocol commands | 27/29 (93.1%) | **28/29 (96.6%)** |
| Protocol actions | 54/85 (63.5%) | **59/85 (69.4%)** |
| Conformance tests | 62 | **73** |

The one remaining uncovered command (`invokeChangesetOperation`) and the eight `changeset/*` actions are covered by the changeset branch, which takes commands to 29/29 once both land.

## Validation

- Full suite: **172 passing, 62 pending, 0 failing**
- Conformance tier stable across repeated consecutive runs
- `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, and hygiene all pass
- Coverage stats regenerated with `npm run test-agent-host-e2e-coverage`

title: Built-in skills are not returned by the sessionless commands.list API (skills unavailable in sessionless chat input completions)
body:
## Summary

The sessionless `commands.list()` API does not return built-in skills. As a result, skills are **not available in the sessionless chat input completions** — they only become available **after a session has been created**.

## Details

- The sessionless `commands.list()` API filters returned commands to those flagged `availableAtSessionStart`.
- Skills are always `availableAtSessionStart: false`, so **no skills appear in that RPC at all** (including built-in skills bundled with the runtime).
- Skills are instead surfaced through a separate API surface — `skills.discover` / `session.skills.list()` and the `session.skills_loaded` event — all of which require (or are tied to) a loaded session.

## Impact

- When a user has not yet created a session (i.e. the sessionless chat input), skill slash commands do not show up in input completions.
- Built-in skills in particular are effectively invisible until a session exists, which is surprising because they ship with the runtime and could reasonably be offered at session start.
- This creates an inconsistent completion experience: built-in commands (e.g. runtime commands) are completable pre-session, but skills are not.

## Expected

Skills (at minimum built-in skills) should be discoverable/completable in the sessionless chat input, or there should be a documented, intentional reason why skill completions require a session.

## Notes

The implementing repository is private, so this issue captures the behavior at a conceptual level rather than linking source. Happy to provide more detail on request.

title: Don't splice signed thinking blocks from different responses when merging assistant messages
body:
## Summary

Fixes #327646. When prompt-tsx drops tool results from older rounds, `keepWith` prunes the paired `tool_use` blocks, leaving consecutive assistant messages whose signed thinking blocks get naïvely concatenated. The Anthropic API rejects the result because thinking blocks from different responses are spliced into one message.

## Fix

Extract `mergeAssistantContent()` from the merge loop in `rawMessagesToMessagesAPI()`. It keeps at most one response's thinking blocks — the one whose `tool_use` survives — hoisted to position 0 so manual thinking mode (`type: "enabled"`) still sees a leading thinking block. When neither half owns a tool call, all thinking is dropped.

dispatchTurnStarted(client, sessionUri, 'turn-1', `terminal-edit:${editedFile}`, 1);
```

No other AHP implementation understands `terminal-edit:`, so the test describes our implementation rather than the protocol. It had to be re-expressed rather than moved.

## What's covered

A conformance-tier suite, `suites/changesetSuite.ts`:

- **Computation status** — subscribing yields a snapshot, and the terminal `ready` status arrives as an action. Asserting only the snapshot would pass without the host ever finishing the computation.
- **An added file** — no before-side, `diff: { added: 1, removed: 0 }`, `reviewed: false`.
- **An edit to a committed file** — both sides present, so a client can render a real diff.
- **Review state** — `changeset/filesReviewChanged` is the one client-dispatchable action on this channel; the server echoes it so other clients converge.
- **The catalog** — each changeset (`branch`, `uncommitted`, `session`) is its own channel, because `changeset/*` actions are scoped to the changeset URI and a session-only subscription never receives them.

Every scenario drives real file changes through **host-executed bang commands**, so the changeset is computed from git rather than from what a tool reported — and nothing crosses the model boundary.

## Coverage

Actions **44/85 (51.8%) → 50/85 (58.8%)**, newly covering `changeset/statusChanged`, `contentChanged`, `filesReviewChanged`, `operationsChanged`, `cleared`, and `chat/activityChanged`.

Three `changeset/*` actions remain, recorded in the README with what each needs: `fileSet`/`fileRemoved` are the incremental per-file updates rather than the bulk path a fresh session takes, and `operationStatusChanged` needs an invoked operation (`commit` and `discard-changes` are the two that run without network).

## Method note

The asserted shapes came from a throwaway probe against a real session, not from reading the service. That's also how I confirmed the **branch** changeset is the one that reports a newly added file — worth stating, because the three changesets emit similar traffic and picking the wrong one yields a test that passes while asserting nothing.

## Validation

Conformance **57 → 62 passing**, stable across three consecutive runs. Copilot 49, Claude 44, Codex 8, 0 failing. Typecheck and hygiene clean.

Independent of [#328077](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328077) and [#328105](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328105).

(Written by Copilot)

title: agentHost: use Responses API for BYOK models
body:
## Summary

- replace the Agent Host BYOK Chat Completions proxy contract with OpenAI Responses
- preserve ordered text, structured reasoning, encrypted reasoning state, function/custom tool calls, usage, and continuation data across the renderer bridge
- support the SDK's default non-streaming Responses path and `stream: true` SSE
- opt into encrypted thinking only for Agent Host BYOK requests so other `vscode.lm` consumers retain their existing behavior
- round-trip OpenAI encrypted reasoning and provider continuation metadata such as Anthropic signatures/redacted thinking and Gemini thought signatures
- preserve all assistant text parts and keep reasoning chunks separated by reasoning ID
- add focused unit coverage and a real Copilot SDK multi-turn reasoning integration test

## Why

The Chat Completions translation loses fidelity for thinking-capable models and tool continuations. Responses provides first-class reasoning and output items that match the Copilot SDK agent loop more closely. Some providers also require opaque reasoning state on later turns; this change carries that state only for the Agent Host BYOK path.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client`
